md_docs_2runtime-settings(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2runtime-settings(3)

NAME

md_docs_2runtime-settings - Runtime settings

Rendering changes apply while a call is running. CLI keyboard controls and the browser settings panel use the same C validation and transaction machinery. Changes affect the viewer who requested them. A viewer cannot change another viewer’s palette, dimensions, colors, or frame rate.

The browser reports when the host accepts a change. Hosts may cap the requested frame rate; the acknowledgment contains the actual value. Saved preferences stay separate from effective remote settings, so a temporary server limit does not rewrite the user’s preferences. Invalid requests leave all prior values intact. Credentials, encryption, authentication, and session administration are outside the rendering endpoint.

Local C transactions

Use options_apply_patch() from ascii-chat/options/runtime.h for related edits: 

options_edit_t edits[] = {


  {.name = "color_mode", .type = OPTIONS_VALUE_INT,


   .value.integer = TERM_COLOR_TRUECOLOR},


  {.name = "fps", .type = OPTIONS_VALUE_INT, .value.integer = 30},
};
options_patch_t patch = {


  .edits = edits, .count = 2,


  .expected_revision = OPTIONS_REVISION_ANY,


  .origin = OPTIONS_ORIGIN_LOCAL,
};
asciichat_error_t error = options_apply_patch(&patch, NULL);

The writer mutex covers reading the latest state, copying it, applying every edit, validating the final candidate, and publishing one immutable snapshot. An invalid field rejects the whole transaction. No-op edits do not advance the revision. Existing typed setters are single-edit transactions.

Use options_toggle(), options_adjust(), or options_cycle() for relative keyboard actions. They compute the new value inside the transaction. When an edit depends on a previously inspected state, capture it with options_read_snapshot() and pass its revision as expected_revision; a stale edit returns ERROR_INVALID_STATE and must be refreshed.

options_revision() lets an owner loop coalesce notifications. Read values and revision together with options_read_snapshot(). Network sends, UI callbacks, and observer notifications happen outside the options writer mutex.

Borrowed options_get() pointers remain valid until options shutdown. Retired snapshots are retained until then: the previous fixed-capacity deferred list could free a snapshot still held by a reader. Retention grows with successful local changes (approximately sizeof(options_t) per change); remote rendering updates use per-participant state and do not retain global snapshots.

Browser state

runtimeOptions(module) returns a store for that specific C/WASM instance. applyPatch() submits one JSON transaction. getSnapshot() returns committed values and revision together. subscribe() observes changes from C keyboard actions as well as JavaScript edits; React uses useSyncExternalStore.

There is no JavaScript palette/flip cache. Renderer and client modules do not replace each other’s options accessors. UI submissions include only fields changed since the preceding submission, preserving intervening engine changes.

Per-participant protocol

All live remote rendering changes use ACIP_SETTINGS_SYNC (6063) and ACIP_SETTINGS_ACK (6064), over the connection’s normal encrypted transport. CLIENT_CAPABILITIES initializes terminal capabilities and advertises codec support. Later codec advertisements cannot overwrite rendering preferences. There is no feature negotiation or alternate runtime settings path. Hosts and clients must both be updated for live rendering controls; older clients that only send capability updates cannot change rendering after initialization.

Each payload begins with five network-order 32-bit integers:

Offset Field Meaning 0 schema 1 4 request Connection-local correlation ID; 0 for initial host state 8 expected_revision Host revision to compare, or UINT32_MAX 12 revision Committed host revision in replies 16 status ASCIICHAT_OK or an asciichat_error_t

The remaining bytes contain a JSON object, limited to 4096 bytes. A header-only request queries effective settings. Allowed fields are width, height, fps, color_mode, color_filter, render_mode, palette_type, palette_custom, and matrix_rain. Unknown fields, duplicate aliases, invalid types, oversized payloads, invalid palettes, and stale revisions are rejected.

The host prepares dimensions, capabilities, and palette together before publishing per-participant render state under its owner mutex. Every validly framed request receives a full effective snapshot, including on rejection. Clients correlate replies within the current connection and commit effective state in C before exposing it to JavaScript.

session_participant_request_settings() submits this request; session_participant_receive_settings() consumes the acknowledgment and invokes the participant callbacks after releasing its settings mutex. It never applies another viewer’s preferences to global options. Requests may retain the default TERM_COLOR_AUTO: the participant resolves it to detected terminal capabilities (or monochrome when detection is unreliable) before validating and sending, without rewriting the caller’s preferences.

Verification

test-runtime-settings is a standalone native test, including Windows. It checks concurrent updates, atomic rejection, revision conflicts, snapshot lifetime, animation exclusion, and independent remote viewers.

On Windows, python tests/integration/runtime_settings_cli.py build/bin/ascii-chat.exe drives real keyboard controls in isolated hidden child consoles over TCP and WebSocket. Browser coverage uses the rebuilt WASM artifacts and an isolated Vite server: vp exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/runtime-settings.config.ts from web/web. It checks native-host/browser rendering, independent viewers, C host requests, invalid transactions, and the shared C keyboard UI.
